newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine firms shelve wheat buying plans.
newsitem.headline: Philippine firms shelve wheat buying plans.

text.p: Philippine flour millers on Friday postponed plans to buy wheat following a de facto devaluation of the peso.
"The is the worst time to place orders...I've cancelled all plans to buy wheat for now until the foreign exchange calms," said an executive in one of the country's largest flour mills.
"I've postponed buying wheat for now," said another executive in a Philippine mill.
The Philippines buys an average of two million tonnes of wheat annually, mainly from the U.S.
The peso hit a low of 29.45 on Friday after the Central Bank announced it was going to allow the peso to move in a new, wider range to quell speculation. The peso closed at 26.401 on Thursday.

"With the peso pegged at 29.45 pesos, the price of a 25-kg bag of flour in the domestic market has to be adjusted to (raised by) between 26 to 30 pesos per bag to reflect additional cost that we have to pay for the wheat and its freight," said a senior trader in a Philippine mill.
The trader said his company was selling soft flour at 245 pesos per 25-kg and hard flour at 285 pesos on Friday.
